# SDK fixture provenance

`draft.ts` was generated by the actual SDK at the head of LiteFlow PR #3, commit `ec8a59083494f1c36b3a2561a60a4a7882404d59`. `generate.py` calls `compile_workflow`, computes the bundle digest with `bundle_digest` and serializes the SDK's `Draft` model. Only the workflow/team IDs and ETag are fixture metadata. The two identical message schemas share one constant to avoid duplicating generated data. The exported Draft retains the complete SDK output

The generation environment used Python 3.13, `openai==2.54.0`, `pydantic==2.14.3` and `httpx==0.28.1`. Pinning these dependencies also pins the generated OpenAI message schemas

From this directory, create an isolated environment and regenerate

```sh
python3.13 -m venv /tmp/liteflow-graph-fixtures
/tmp/liteflow-graph-fixtures/bin/pip install \
  'liteflow @ git+https://github.com/BerriAI/liteflow.git@ec8a59083494f1c36b3a2561a60a4a7882404d59' \
  'openai==2.54.0' 'pydantic==2.14.3' 'httpx==0.28.1'
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 /tmp/liteflow-graph-fixtures/bin/python generate.py
../../../../../scripts/with_dashboard_node.sh npx prettier --write draft.ts
```

The email reply example covers both node types, previous-step references, a literal Python argument, input/output schemas, structured ChatCompletion output and retry configuration

`WorkflowGraphDemo.tsx` supplies these bundles to the production components. Its execution overlays and unsupported-node example are explicitly synthetic. The demo imports fixtures only through a route guarded by `NODE_ENV === "development"`
